label: First two copy-phase inputs (recall_idx 1-2) in longer sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely on the first two copied tokens fed back in (input = orig(0) at recall_idx 1, orig(1) at recall_idx 2). recall_idx 1 holds 64% of the activation mass and recall_idx 2 holds 33%. Rate goes up with sequence length: rare for L=3-4, about 0.12 of steps for L>=7. It never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on the first occurrence of a token. Magnitude: the largest activations are at recall_idx 1 when the input/first token is b (b is 3x lift and the top examples are all b at recall_idx 1). recall_idx 1 is usually stronger than recall_idx 2. There is a weak tail on later copy steps (recall_idx >= 3, about 3% of mass). Most misses are low-magnitude firings in short sequences (L 4-5).

issues: The core claims check out. On dev, all activation is in the copy phase (original and delimiter steps have rate 0). recall_idx 1 holds 63.5% of activation mass and recall_idx 2 holds 33.1%. Firing happens only when in_first==0. The top examples are all 'b' at recall_idx 1. On test, the original predicate scores P 0.803, R 0.811, F1 0.807, MR 0.894, matching the report.

Missed systematic class: a copy-phase input of 'b' fires at ANY position, not only at recall_idx 1. (recall_idx>=3)&(in_tok==b) has precision 0.499, against 0.010 for other tokens at recall_idx>=3. Other high-lift tokens do not show this (v: 0.07, u: 0.04). The 'b' steps make up about 4.4% of active steps and are most of the 'weak tail on later copy steps'. The explanation calls that tail generic noise and ties 'b' only to recall_idx 1.

The L>=6 cutoff stands in for a graded effect that depends on how many outputs remain (to_go), not a hard length threshold. Firing rates by recall_idx/L are: r1: L3 0.14, L4 0.26, L5 0.51, L6 0.75, L7 0.91, L8 0.97, L9 0.99. r2: L5 0.17, L6 0.41, L7 0.65, L8 0.82, L9 0.92. As a result, recall_idx 1 at L=5 (precision 0.505, 6.3% of active steps) is a systematic miss, and recall_idx 2 at L=6 (precision 0.41) is a systematic false-positive block. The test misses output shows exactly these. This is a fuzzy boundary rather than a wrong concept.
Small overclaim: 'rare for L=3-4' fits recall_idx 2, but recall_idx 1 still fires 26% of the time at L=4 and 14% at L=3.
